Independent symbolic verification of the r³ variance coefficient and both r² logarithmic endpoint coefficients, plus 90-digit direct C_k checks at k=20,40,80,160,320,640,1000,2000,5000,10000. The analytic argument, not finite tests, establishes the result.
correctness.rationale: With r=1/k and unit scale, write X=e^{rY}, Y=log E, E~Exp(1). The cumulant generating function of Y is logΓ(1+t). Its cubic expansion gives μ=-γ, v=ζ(2)=a² and κ3=-2ζ(3). Hence m_r=1+μr+(μ²+v)r²/2+O(r³), s_r²=vr²+(2μv+κ3)r³+O(r⁴), and s_r=ar+a(μ−ζ(3)/v)r²+O(r³). Thus r^{-1}log(m_r−s_r)=μ−a+(ζ(3)/a)r+O(r²) and r^{-1}log(m_r+s_r)=μ+a−(ζ(3)/a)r+O(r²). Smooth Taylor expansion of F_Y(y)=1−exp(−exp y) at these two endpoints yields C_k=Cinf−A/k+O(k^{-2}), with strictly positive A. Because Cinf exceeds erf(1/sqrt2), eventual recovery above the Gaussian one-sigma benchmark follows. The lower endpoint m_r−s_r is positive for sufficiently small r. No global monotonicity, minimal K or exact finite crossing is claimed.
residual_risks: Expansion applies as k→∞ to every positive real shape and arbitrary positive scale; it is not a uniform global bound for all k>0.
Finite high-precision arithmetic and pre-existing VERIFY_OK logs do not themselves prove the remainder.

value.rationale: The same one-sigma functional previously fails its Gaussian comparison for the non-infinitely-divisible shape k=3 and is evaluated only numerically for shape up to 10. The large-shape boundary is a mathematically natural question: the theorem identifies the reflected-Gumbel endpoint, the positive exact Apéry correction determining its approach from below, and eventual recovery above the Gaussian benchmark. This quantifies a motivated signed endpoint law and gives a precise asymptotic benchmark for subsequent finite-shape investigations; it is not a claim of a global phase diagram or an arbitrary parameter slice. Although elementary Gamma expansions are proof ingredients, the prior source does not specify their combination at the standardized moving one-sigma endpoints.
residual_risks: The derivation is a relatively short application of classical Gamma cumulants; mathematical value rests specifically on the previously identified failure-and-recovery question and signed quantitative endpoint, not on new general asymptotic machinery.
